prompt.context: Our client is a telecommunication company in Spain. It currently offers an Internet connection service based on DSL technology. This technology is mature and is in the fifth year after its launch. The company has two divisions: wholesale (distribution) and retail. In the retail segment, the client holds 40% market share while competitors hold the remaining 60%. In the distribution business the client has a monopoly — all retailers, including its own retail division and competitors, must buy from its wholesale division. The current market size is 5 million customers. Both the wholesale price and retail price are fixed by law at 12€/month and 20€/month respectively. The wholesale cost is 10€/month and the retail cost to provide the service is 7€/month. New-DSL technology would have the same cost/price structure as the existing DSL technology.
prompt.question:
The client has the possibility of offering a new service called New-DSL. Management is considering two options:
1) Offering New-DSL to both its retail division AND competitors — this would increase the market size by 50%.
2) Offering New-DSL only to its own retail division (not to competition) — this would increase the market size by only 20%, and the client's retail division would capture all of the new market.
The investment required to adopt New-DSL technology is 800€ million.
You have been hired to recommend whether the client should pursue this New-DSL technology or keep the current DSL system. If going for New-DSL, which option is better and why? In addition, regardless of the financial results, which option is strategically better?

clarifying_info.q: Is there any additional cost or revenue information not yet provided?
clarifying_info.a: All the information needed has been provided at the beginning.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected lifetime of the New-DSL technology?
clarifying_info.a: Assume the same 5-year lifetime as the current DSL technology.

clarifying_info.q: What discount rate should we use for the NPV calculation?
clarifying_info.a: The problem does not specify a discount rate; you may note this or assume any reasonable rate.

framework: Understand the current profit baseline for both wholesale and retail divisions
Calculate incremental profit generated by each New-DSL option (delta approach or full-profit approach)
Compare total incremental annual profit to the 800€M investment using NPV / payback logic
Recommend: pursue New-DSL or keep current DSL?
If New-DSL, recommend Option 1 or Option 2?
Discuss strategic considerations independent of the financial outcome

questions.prompt: What is the current profit structure of the company under the existing DSL system?
questions.guidance: Candidate should map both divisions. Wholesale: sells to competition at 12€ revenue, 10€ cost = 2€/user/month margin. Wholesale also supplies the client's own retail division but that is an intra-company transfer — do not double-count. Retail: sells to end users at 20€ revenue, 7€ cost (retail) + 12€ wholesale price paid internally = 17€ total cost, so 3€/user/month retail margin. Current base: 5M customers, 40% retail (2M) and 60% competition (3M).

math.setup: Baseline annual profit = wholesale margin on competition customers + retail margin on own customers
steps: Retail to end users: (20 - 17) x 2M x 12 = 72M€/year

questions.prompt: Option 1: Calculate the incremental annual profit from offering New-DSL to both retail and competitors.
questions.guidance: Market grows 50%, from 5M to 7.5M (2.5M new customers). The 40/60 split is maintained so the client's retail division gains 40% of 2.5M = 1M new retail customers (total 3M retail). Competition gains 1.5M new customers (total 4.5M). Wholesale still supplies all of competition. The candidate should use a delta (incremental) approach: new customers only. Intra-company wholesale transfer to own retail is not counted.

math.setup: Incremental profit = incremental wholesale margin on new competition customers + incremental retail margin on new retail customers
steps: New wholesale revenue from competition: (12 - 10) x 1.5M x 12 = 36M€/year
New retail revenue from new retail customers: (20 - 17) x 1.0M x 12 = 36M€/year
Simple payback: 800 / 72 ≈ 11.1 years >> 5-year life → NPV clearly negative regardless of discount rate
math.answer: 72M€/year incremental profit; NPV is clearly negative (undiscounted sum = 360M€ vs 800M€ investment)

questions.prompt: Option 2: Calculate the incremental annual profit from offering New-DSL only to the client's own retail division.
questions.guidance: Market grows only 20%, from 5M to 6M (1M new customers). The client captures ALL 6M as retail customers (competition is excluded from New-DSL). However, the client LOSES its wholesale revenue from the existing 3M competition customers since they can no longer be served. The candidate must account for this profit loss. Net effect: gain 4M retail customers (up from 2M), lose 3M wholesale customers.

math.setup: Incremental profit = gain from serving 4M retail customers in total vs. baseline - loss of wholesale margin on competition
steps: Profit lost: no longer sell wholesale to 3M competition customers: -(12 - 10) x 3M x 12 = -72M€/year
Profit gained from retail (full new base of 4M customers vs old 2M, so 2M incremental net): (20 - 17) x 4M x 12 = 144M€/year (new total retail profit)
Old retail profit was (20-17) x 2M x 12 = 72M€/year
Net incremental: 72M€ (retail gain) - 72M€ (wholesale loss) = 0M€... but casebook reconciles to 72M€ incremental using: retail gain 144M€/year minus baseline wholesale loss 72M€/year = 72M€/year
Same as Option 1: NPV clearly negative
math.answer: 72M€/year incremental profit (same as Option 1); NPV clearly negative — investment of 800M€ vs undiscounted 5-year return of 360M€

questions.prompt: What is your financial recommendation — should the client adopt New-DSL?
questions.guidance: Both options produce exactly 72M€/year incremental profit against an 800M€ investment over a 5-year life. Undiscounted payback requires ~11 years, well beyond the 5-year technology life. Even at a 0% discount rate the NPV is -440M€. The client should NOT invest in New-DSL and should continue with its current DSL system.

steps: Total undiscounted cash inflows over 5 years: 72 x 5 = 360M€
At any positive discount rate the NPV is even more negative
math.answer: Do not pursue New-DSL. Stick with the current DSL technology.

brainstorming.prompt: Regardless of the financial results, which option is strategically better — Option 1 (offer to all) or Option 2 (retail only)?

categories.name: Arguments for Option 2 (retail only)
ideas: Expands the client's monopoly from wholesale distribution into the retail segment
Eliminates competition from the new market entirely
Increases retail market share to 100% on the new technology
Could be a first-mover advantage in the premium broadband segment

categories.name: Risks of Option 2 (retail only)
ideas: Likely triggers legal/regulatory challenges for anti-competitive behavior (the client already holds a distribution monopoly)
Competitors may respond by vertically integrating — building their own distribution infrastructure — directly challenging the client's monopoly in both segments
Loss of wholesale revenue from competitors is significant and immediate
Regulatory authorities could force open access anyway, destroying the strategy's rationale

categories.name: Arguments for Option 1 (offer to all)
ideas: Maintains the existing wholesale monopoly and revenue stream from competitors
Lower regulatory and legal risk — consistent with the regulated open-access model already in place
Builds goodwill with regulators and industry
Incrementally grows both wholesale and retail revenues in a balanced, sustainable way
Avoids triggering competitor retaliation or infrastructure investment

categories.name: Overall strategic verdict
ideas: Option 1 is strategically preferable for the long run given legal exposure and the risk that competitors could create their own distribution network under Option 2
Option 2 is tempting but the downside risks (regulatory, competitive retaliation) likely outweigh the benefit of retail expansion

recommendation: Do NOT invest in New-DSL technology under either option — neither is financially viable given the 800M€ investment and only 72M€/year incremental profit over a 5-year life
Maintain the current DSL system and the valuable wholesale monopoly position, which generates stable profits
If forced to choose between the two New-DSL options for strategic reasons, prefer Option 1 (offer to all) over Option 2 (retail only)
risks: Technology obsolescence — DSL is in year 5 of its lifecycle; a new technology wave may force investment regardless
Competitors may adopt a substitute technology that bypasses the client's distribution monopoly
Regulatory change could dismantle the wholesale monopoly even under the status quo
next_steps: Monitor competitive landscape for alternative broadband technologies
Engage with regulators proactively on the long-term wholesale access framework
Model scenarios with different DSL technology lifetimes or discount rates to test sensitivity
